text: A one percent fee can take more than you ever put in.
It's legal. It's disclosed. And you'd never feel it. So how?
Two funds. Same— literally the same investments. One charges one percent more a year.
Hit like if that sounds like nothing. It's supposed to.
Five hundred a month, forty years. Say both earn seven percent, that's an assumption.
Ten years in, the gap's forty-six hundred bucks. Whatever, right?
Send this to the friend who's never checked their fees.
Year twenty? Twenty-nine grand. Okay, that's a car. Year thirty? A hundred seven grand.
Year forty's next. Follow, 'cause this page catches the quiet ones.
That one percent cost you three hundred sixteen grand.
You only put in two forty. The fee beat you.
So… still call one percent small?
